title: Pre-Shipment Quality Control & Third-Party Factory Audits in Türkiye
seoTitle: Quality Control Turkey Sourcing: Audits & Payment Guide
metaDescription: How to run pre-shipment quality control and factory audits in Türkiye with SGS, Intertek, MERSİS checks, and safe LC, CAD, or 30% deposit terms.
quickAnswer: Foreign buyers sourcing textiles, machinery, furniture, or food from Türkiye should hire accredited inspectors such as SGS or Intertek for During-Production Checks (DUPRO) and Final Random Inspections (FRI) before releasing final balances. Pairing milestone payments, Letters of Credit, or CAD with MERSİS registry verification prevents quality disputes and intermediary fraud.

body.text: When should foreign buyers hire SGS, Intertek or independent inspectors before final payment?

Book a third-party inspection at three distinct triggers: a Factory Audit before paying a deposit to a new supplier, a During-Production Check (DUPRO) when 20–40% of goods are finished on complex orders, and a Final Random Inspection (FRI) plus Container Loading Supervision once 80–100% of cartons are packed—strictly before wiring the final balance.

Major accredited testing, inspection, and certification (TIC) firms maintain deep nationwide coverage across Istanbul, Bursa, İzmir, Denizli, Gaziantep, and Kayseri. [SGS Türkiye](https://www.sgs.com/en-tr/services/product-inspection) holds TÜRKAK accreditations under ISO/IEC 17020 and 17025 for Initial Production Checks (IPC), DUPRO, FRI, and Loading Supervision, while [Intertek Türkiye](https://www.intertek.com/contact/ema/turkey/) provides factory evaluations, social-compliance audits, and laboratory testing. Independent sector-specialist inspectors also work well for bespoke apparel, marble, or industrial machinery where deep niche engineering knowledge matters.
What payment terms (30% deposit, LC, CAD) protect both sides in Turkish trade?

Three structures dominate Turkish export trade: a 30% Telegraphic Transfer (T/T) deposit with 70% balance against a passed FRI report and Bill of Lading copy; an Irrevocable Letter of Credit (LC under ICC UCP 600) for larger orders; and Cash Against Documents (CAD / D/P) for repeat buyers seeking lower bank fees than an LC.

As detailed in [Turkish foreign trade payment guides](https://www.atc.org.tr/en/foreign-trade-guide/dis-ticaret-odeme-sekilleri/) and [UCP 600 / URC 522 trade finance summaries](https://www.artagandijital.com/en/knowledge/payment-methods-letter-of-credit.html), tying final T/T release or LC document presentation to a clean third-party inspection certificate aligns both parties' incentives.

We organize factory-audit itineraries, ground transport, and vetted introductions; formal sales contracts, LC compliance, tax checks, and customs procedures belong strictly to licensed Turkish attorneys, SMMMs (CPAs), trade banks, and accredited inspection bodies.
How do you verify export licenses and past shipping references?

Verify a Turkish supplier's legal identity through the Ministry of Trade's [MERSİS central registry](https://mersis.ticaret.gov.tr/) and the [TOBB Turkish Trade Registry Gazette (TTSG)](https://www.tobb.org.tr/TurkiyeTicaretSicilGazetesi/Sayfalar/Eng/AnaSayfa.php) to confirm active status, paid-in capital, and authorized signatories. Next, check membership in a regional Exporters' Association under the [Türkiye Exporters Assembly (TİM)](https://tim.org.tr/en/about-tim-about-us) and request redacted Bills of Lading or EUR.1 movement certificates from recent shipments.

Every Turkish commercial exporter must belong to a sectoral Exporters' Association under TİM to issue export customs declarations. Matching the beneficiary bank account name against the exact MERSİS legal entity title—and confirming that the signatory on your proforma invoice appears on the company's notarized signature circular (imza sirküleri)—eliminates most shell-company risk before any deposit leaves your account.
What red flags signal unreliable suppliers?

Key warning signs include refusing third-party SGS or Intertek access, requesting deposits into personal or third-country bank accounts, quoting prices far below raw-material benchmarks, and stalling when asked for a live factory walkthrough. Other red flags include mismatched MERSİS addresses, expired ISO or CE certificates, and pressure to waive formal inspection clauses before loading.
Run through this due-diligence checklist prior to issuing a purchase order:

items: Legal identity match: Verify the supplier's tax ID, MERSİS record, and authorized signatory against the proforma invoice.
Bank account alignment: Wire funds only to a Turkish corporate bank account bearing the exact registered company name.
Inspection clause in contract: State AQL defect limits and mandatory FRI pass requirements directly in the purchase agreement.
On-site physical audit: Visit the production floor in person or dispatch an accredited auditor before committing to repeat volume.
Reference verification: Confirm at least two recent export shipments (EUR.1, ATR, or redacted B/L) to comparable markets.

faq.q: When is the best stage to book a Final Random Inspection (FRI) in Türkiye?
faq.a: Schedule a Final Random Inspection once 100% of production is complete and at least 80% of the order is packed in export cartons, always before releasing the final balance payment.

faq.q: How can a foreign buyer verify if a Turkish factory is legally registered?
faq.a: Cross-check the company's legal title, MERSİS number, and authorized signatories through the Ministry of Trade MERSİS portal, the Turkish Trade Registry Gazette (TTSG), and the relevant chamber of commerce.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Letter of Credit (LC) and Cash Against Documents (CAD)?
faq.a: An LC carries an irrevocable bank payment guarantee when compliant shipping documents are presented, whereas CAD relies on banks releasing title documents upon buyer payment without a bank guarantee.

faq.q: Are SGS and Intertek accredited inside Türkiye?
faq.a: Yes. Both SGS Türkiye (operating since 1933, TÜRKAK-accredited under ISO/IEC 17020 and 17025) and Intertek Türkiye operate nationwide inspection, lab-testing, and factory-audit networks.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye conduct technical quality inspections or draft trade contracts?
faq.a: No. We coordinate factory visit itineraries, transport, interpreters, and independent introductions; accredited inspection bodies perform QC audits, while Turkish trade attorneys and banks handle contracts and LCs.

faq.q: What is a common warning sign of a trading intermediary posing as a Turkish factory?
faq.a: Reluctance to allow an unannounced or third-party inspector onto the production floor, mismatched factory and invoice addresses, or inability to show machinery and active production lines during a site visit.
